nodes.description: EMG1 is a small subunit processome factor required for 18S rRNA maturation and 40S subunit production, in addition to catalysing N1-methylation of the pseudouridine at the m1acp3-pseudouridine site of 18S rRNA. In yeast the assembly-factor role and the methyltransferase role are separable. In patient lymphoblasts and fibroblasts, 18S rRNA processing is slightly but consistently delayed, although steady-state 40S levels and global protein synthesis are not detectably reduced in these cells.

evidence.reference_title: Mutation of EMG1 causing Bowen-Conradi syndrome results in reduced cell proliferation rates concomitant with G2/M arrest and 18S rRNA processing delay.
evidence.snippet: The rate of 18S rRNA processing was consistently delayed in patient cells, although this did not lead to a difference in the levels of 40S ribosomes, or a change in protein synthesis rates.

evidence.reference_title: Novel stress-responsive genes EMG1 and NOP14 encode conserved, interacting proteins required for 40S ribosome biogenesis.
evidence.snippet: We conclude that Emg1 and Nop14 are novel proteins whose interaction is required for the maturation of the 18S rRNA and for 40S ribosome production.

evidence.reference_title: The Bowen-Conradi syndrome protein Nep1 (Emg1) has a dual role in eukaryotic ribosome biogenesis, as an essential assembly factor and in the methylation of Ψ1191 in yeast 18S rRNA.
evidence.snippet: This strongly suggests a dual Nep1 function, as Ψ1191-methyltransferase and ribosome assembly factor.

evidence.reference_title: The ribosome assembly factor Nep1 responsible for Bowen-Conradi syndrome is a pseudouridine-N1-specific methyltransferase.
evidence.snippet: Thus, Nep1 is the first identified example of an N1-specific pseudouridine methyltransferase.

evidence.reference_title: A locus for Bowen-Conradi syndrome maps to chromosome region 12p13.3.
evidence.snippet: By linkage and haplotype analysis the BCS locus was mapped to a 3.5 cM segment (1.9 Mbp) in chromosome region 12p13.3 bounded by F8VWF and D12S397.

evidence.reference_title: Mutation of a gene essential for ribosome biogenesis, EMG1, causes Bowen-Conradi syndrome.
evidence.snippet: In BCS patient fibroblasts, EMG1 mRNA levels did not differ from those of normal cells, but EMG1 protein was dramatically reduced in comparison to that of normal controls.

nodes.description: The Asp86Gly substitution does not reduce EMG1 mRNA but sharply reduces EMG1 protein. The mutant protein shows increased self-association and RNA binding, accumulates in nuclear foci and is degraded by the proteasome. Its catalytic activity, the N1-methylation of the 18S rRNA pseudouridine, is preserved in vitro.

evidence.snippet: The BCS mutation in EMG1 leads to reduced nucleolar localisation, accumulation of EMG1D86G in nuclear foci and its proteasome-dependent degradation.

evidence.reference_title: The Bowen-Conradi syndrome protein Nep1 (Emg1) has a dual role in eukaryotic ribosome biogenesis, as an essential assembly factor and in the methylation of Ψ1191 in yeast 18S rRNA.
evidence.snippet: Interestingly, the Nep1 methyltransferase activity is not affected upon introduction of the BCS mutation. Instead, the mutated protein shows enhanced dimerization propensity and increased affinity for its RNA-target in vitro.

nodes.description: Knock-in of the human founder substitution. Homozygous embryos are small for gestational age, have neural tube defects and die between E8.5 and E12.5, so the allele is more severe in mouse than in human.

Constitutive Emg1 knockout. Homozygous null embryos arrest at the morula stage, fail to form a blastocyst, show defective nucleologenesis and early lineage specification and degenerate before implantation; no homozygotes are found from E8.5 onwards. Loss of p53 does not rescue the arrest.

evidence.reference_title: The Bowen-Conradi syndrome -- a highly lethal autosomal recessive syndrome of microcephaly, micrognathia, low birth weight, and joint deformities.
evidence.snippet: Our additional cases confirm that the major features of the syndrome include porportionate intrauterine growth retardation, microcephaly, micrognathia, a prominent nose, rocker-bottom feet, joint limitation, and failure to thrive, with death within the first year of life.

nodes.description: EMG1 is imported into the nucleus by importins, which also act as chaperones, and is recruited to nucleoli as part of a subcomplex with NOP14, NOC4L and UTP14A. The mutant protein is released from the import complex, aggregates in the nucleus and reaches the nucleolus less efficiently, so less EMG1 is available to the small subunit processome. One study in patient fibroblasts did not detect a change in nucleolar localization, so the extent of this step in patient cells is uncertain.

evidence.snippet: Here, we identify the pre-ribosomal factors NOP14, NOC4L and UTP14A as members of a nucleolar subcomplex that contains EMG1 and is required for its recruitment to nucleoli.

evidence.reference_title: The Bowen-Conradi syndrome protein Nep1 (Emg1) has a dual role in eukaryotic ribosome biogenesis, as an essential assembly factor and in the methylation of Ψ1191 in yeast 18S rRNA.
evidence.snippet: Furthermore, the BCS mutation prevents nucleolar accumulation of Nep1, which could be the reason for reduced growth in yeast and the Bowen-Conradi syndrome.

evidence.snippet: The D86G substitution did not interfere with EMG1 nucleolar localization.

nodes.description: Patient lymphoblasts proliferate more slowly and accumulate in G2/M, while patient fibroblasts proliferate normally. Homozygous D86G knock-in mouse embryos show dramatically reduced cell proliferation, as do autopsy brain and bone marrow from patients, and embryo-derived fibroblasts contain many binucleated cells, pointing to a defect in mitotic progression. The defect does not appear to run through TP53: TP53 and p21 were not increased in patient lymphoblasts, and loss of p53 did not rescue Emg1-null mouse embryos.

nodes.description: The Hutterite founder missense variant, reported as NM_006331.6:c.400A>G in the gene discovery paper and as c.257A>G in later work from the same group, which uses a different reference transcript. It segregated with disease, was absent from 414 non-Hutterite alleles and replaces a highly conserved aspartate predicted to form a salt bridge with Arg84. EMG1 mRNA is normal in patient fibroblasts but EMG1 protein is dramatically reduced.

evidence.reference_title: Mutation of a gene essential for ribosome biogenesis, EMG1, causes Bowen-Conradi syndrome.
evidence.snippet: We identified variant NM_006331.6:c.400A-->G, p.D86G in the 18S ribosome assembly protein EMG1 as the probable cause of BCS. This mutation segregated with disease, was not found in 414 non-Hutterite alleles, and altered a highly conserved aspartic acid (D) residue.

evidence.reference_title: Growth arrest in the ribosomopathy, Bowen-Conradi syndrome, is due to dramatically reduced cell proliferation and a defect in mitotic progression.
evidence.snippet: It is caused by a c.257A>G, p.D86G substitution in the ribosomal biogenesis protein, Essential for Mitotic Growth 1 (EMG1).
